children: Genel Energy said it agreed to buy Capricorn Energy in a $436 million cash deal after hiking its offer price and outbidding Norway-listed DNO.

Genel said Friday that Capricorn shareholders would receive a cash payment of $5.74 for each share. This comprises $4.75 plus a special dividend of 99 cents. The offer represents a 63% premium to the stock's closing price on March 10, the day before Capricorn said it had received separate, non-binding takeover proposals from Alamadiyaf al-Masiyyah for Trading LLC.
Since then, Genel and DNO have been competing to acquire the U.K.-based oil and gas exploration and production company.
In mid-September, DNO revised the terms of its $396 million offer to make it an all-cash deal by removing the payment of a special dividend.

Genel said its new offer represents a roughly 10% premium to DNO's revised offer. Capricorn's management has withdrawn its recommendation that shareholders accept the DNO offer in favor of its own offer, Genel said.

Genel's first offer in early July valued Capricorn at $360 million and proposed paying $4.74 a share in cash. DNO countered with an offer that would have seen Capricorn shareholders receive $5.214 for each share they own, comprising $4.224 in cash and a special dividend of 99 cents.
